q: What are the different types of large cents?
What is a half cent?
What is the Flying Eagle cent?
What is the Indian Head cent?
What are the key dates for early US copper coins?
What is the 1793 chain cent?
What is the 1856 Flying Eagle cent?
large cent half cent Flying Eagle Indian Head 1793 chain cent 1856
a: Early US copper coinage includes half cents (minted 1793-1857 in Liberty Cap, Draped Bust, and Classic Head types) and large cents (1793-1857 in Flowing Hair/Chain, Liberty Cap, Draped Bust, and Classic Head/Coronet types), both struck from pure copper and measuring about the size of modern half dollars. The small cent era began with the Flying Eagle cent (1856-1858, designed by James Longacre), followed by the Indian Head cent (1859-1909, featuring a Liberty head with a Native American feather headdress, issued in copper-nickel 1859-1864 and bronze 1864-1909). Key rarities include the 1793 chain cent (the first US cent, featuring a chain of 15 link rings on the reverse, worth tens of thousands even in low grade), the 1856 Flying Eagle cent (a pattern struck for circulation with about 2,000 minted), and the 1877 Indian Head cent (the lowest mintage of the series at 852,500).

q: What are the different types of Lincoln cents?
What is the Wheat cent reverse?
What is the Lincoln Memorial cent?
What is the Lincoln Shield cent?
What is the 1909-S VDB Lincoln cent?
What is the 1943 steel cent?
What is the 1955 doubled die Lincoln cent?
Lincoln cent Wheat cent Memorial cent Shield cent 1909-S VDB 1943 steel
a: Lincoln cents, first issued in 1909 for the centennial of Lincoln's birth by designer Victor David Brenner, have three major reverse types: Lincoln Wheat (1909-1958, with two wheat stalks), Lincoln Memorial (1959-2008, featuring the Memorial building, designed by Frank Gasparro), and Lincoln Shield (2010-present, with a Union Shield design). Key dates include the 1909-S VDB (San Francisco mint with Brenner's initials, lowest mintage at 484,000), the 1914-D, 1931-S, and the 1943 steel cent (zinc-coated steel to conserve copper for WWII, most showing rust today). The 1955 doubled die is the most famous US error coin, and the 1943 transitional bronze cent (a few copper planchets accidentally struck with 1943 dies) is one of the rarest US coins with about a dozen known, each worth over $100,000.

q: What are the different types of US nickels?
What is a Shield nickel?
What is a Liberty Head nickel?
What is a Buffalo nickel?
What is a Jefferson nickel?
What is the 1913 Liberty Head nickel?
What are key date Buffalo and Jefferson nickels?
Shield nickel Liberty Head Buffalo nickel Jefferson nickel 1913 Liberty Head
a: US five-cent nickels have four major design types: the Shield nickel (1866-1883, with a Union Shield obverse and large '5' in stars on the reverse), the Liberty Head or 'V' nickel (1883-1913, featuring a Liberty head and Roman numeral 'V'), the Buffalo nickel (1913-1938, designed by James Earle Fraser with a Native American profile and American bison, one of the most iconic US coin designs), and the Jefferson nickel (1938-present, with a portrait of Jefferson and his home Monticello). The legendary 1913 Liberty Head nickel—only five exist, all struck secretly after the design was replaced by the Buffalo nickel—sold for over $4.5 million in 2018 and is one of the most famous US rarities. Key Jefferson nickel varieties include the 1939-D and 1939-S with reverse of 1940, the 1950-D with the lowest mintage, and the 2004 Westward Journey series.

q: What are the different designs of US dimes?
What are the major US quarter designs?
What are the major half dollar types?
What is the Mercury dime?
What is the Standing Liberty quarter?
What is the Walking Liberty half dollar?
What is the Barber coinage series?
Mercury dime Standing Liberty quarter Walking Liberty half dollar Barber coinage
a: US silver coinage includes dimes (Draped Bust 1796-1807, Capped Bust 1809-1837, Seated Liberty 1837-1891, Barber 1892-1916, Mercury/Winged Liberty 1916-1945, Roosevelt 1946-present), quarters (Draped Bust 1796-1807, Capped Bust 1815-1838, Seated Liberty 1838-1891, Barber 1892-1916, Standing Liberty 1916-1930, Washington 1932-1998, State Quarters 1999-2008, America the Beautiful 2010-2021, American Women 2022-present), and half dollars (Flowing Hair 1794-1795, Draped Bust 1796-1807, Capped Bust 1807-1839, Seated Liberty 1839-1891, Barber 1892-1915, Walking Liberty 1916-1947, Franklin 1948-1963, Kennedy 1964-present). The Mercury dime (actually Winged Liberty representing freedom of thought) and Walking Liberty half dollar are both by Adolph A. Weinman and are considered among the most beautiful US coin designs, while the Standing Liberty quarter by Hermon MacNeil has an exposed date that wore off quickly, making full-date examples scarce.

q: What are the different types of US dollar coins?
What is a Morgan dollar?
What is a Peace dollar?
What is an Eisenhower dollar?
What is the Sacagawea dollar?
What are Presidential dollars?
What is the 1804 silver dollar?
Morgan dollar Peace dollar Eisenhower Sacagawea Presidential 1804 dollar
a: US dollar coins include early silver dollars (Flowing Hair 1794-1795, Draped Bust 1795-1804, Seated Liberty 1840-1873), the Morgan dollar (1878-1904 and 1921, designed by George T. Morgan, one of the most collected US series with 95 date-mint combinations), the Peace dollar (1921-1935, by Anthony de Francisci, symbolizing peace after WWI), the Eisenhower dollar (1971-1978, honoring the president and Apollo 11), the Susan B. Anthony dollar (1979-1999, the first US coin depicting a real woman), the Sacagawea dollar (2000-present, featuring the Shoshone guide with her infant son), and the Presidential dollar series (2007-2016, each deceased president in order). The famous 1804 silver dollar was actually struck in the 1830s for diplomatic presentation sets—only 15 exist, and one sold for $7.68 million in 2021, making it one of the most valuable US coins.
